 Print Chief minister Hemant Soren addresses the media after the cabinet meeting on Wednesday Ranchi: The Hemant Soren-led cabinet on Wednesday approved a 3% hike in dearness allowance (DA) for state govt employees, raising it from 60% to 63% with effect from July 1, 2026. It also approved a corresponding increase in dearness relief (DR) for pensioners and family pensioners. The decision, taken at a meeting chaired by Hemant, will benefit employees covered under the 7th, 6th and 5th Pay Commissions. The cabinet also approved a long-pending revision of the pay grade of 19 welfare department employees who were promoted from chowkidar to block welfare supervisor. Their grade pay will be increased from Rs 1,900 to Rs 2,400 in compliance with a Jharkhand high court order. The cabinet considered 41 proposals. Among other decisions, it sanctioned Rs 37.36 crore for the construction of a degree college at Bishrampur under Nilamber-Pitamber University in Palamu district. It also approved Rs 85.73 crore for the Karmatand market bypass road in Jamtara, Rs 48.78 crore for reconstruction of the Patkum-Ichagarh-Patpur Canal-Dulsidih-Laba road in Seraikela-Kharsawan, Rs 44.53 crore for widening and strengthening a road in Pakur, and Rs 28.77 crore for reconstruction of roads in Ranchi district.  In the social sector, the cabinet approved Rs 10 crore from the Jharkhand Contingency Fund for ex gratia assistance to families affected by lightning strikes. It also extended the National Health Mission in the state until March 31, 2027. The cabinet approved amendments to the Registration Act through the Jharkhand Amendment Bill, 2026. It also banned fresh appointments of computer operators and data entry operators in the secretariat and its attached offices. Funds were also sanctioned for irrigation, judicial, mining and e-courts-related initiatives.
